precepts.text: A statute for ever: in the seventh month, on the tenth day, ye shall afflict your souls, and the priest made an atonement to cleanse you from all your sins before the Lord.
precepts.point: Isaiah 53 cannot be speaking of David, who was already dead in Isaiah's day; it speaks of Jesus Christ, cut off out of the land of the living for the transgression of the people, the ultimate sacrifice.

note.label: Numbers 29: The Feasts of the Seventh Month

precepts.why:
The tenth day of the seventh month is an holy convocation, a large gathering, wherein “ye shall afflict your souls: ye shall not do any work therein.” This is the day of atonement, and Leviticus 16 institutes it.

“And this shall be a statute for ever unto you: that in the seventh month, on the tenth day of the month, ye shall afflict your souls, and do no work at all, whether it be one of your own country, or a stranger that sojourneth among you: For on that day shall the priest make an atonement for you, to cleanse you, that ye may be clean from all your sins before the Lord.”

A statute for ever: on that day the priest made an atonement to cleanse the people from all their sins before the Lord. “It shall be a sabbath of rest unto you, and ye shall afflict your souls, by a statute for ever.” That is the sin offering of atonement the offerings of Numbers 29 are laid beside.

precepts.text: The fast that the Lord has chosen is a day for a man to afflict his soul, to loose the bands of wickedness, and to break every yoke.
precepts.point: Isaiah 53 cannot be speaking of David, who was already dead in Isaiah's day; it speaks of Jesus Christ, cut off out of the land of the living for the transgression of the people, the ultimate sacrifice.

note.label: Numbers 29: The Feasts of the Seventh Month

precepts.why:
“ye shall afflict your souls.” To afflict your soul is to fast. “Is it such a fast that I have chosen? a day for a man to afflict his soul? is it to bow down his head as a bulrush, and to spread sackcloth and ashes under him? wilt thou call this a fast, and an acceptable day to the Lord?”

“Is not this the fast that I have chosen? to loose the bands of wickedness, to undo the heavy burdens, and to let the oppressed go free, and that ye break every yoke?” The fast the Lord has chosen is a day for a man to afflict his soul, to loose the bands of wickedness, to undo the heavy burdens, to let the oppressed go free, and to break every yoke.

That is why we still fast on this day once a year, and why we go out and teach on the day of atonement.

precepts.text: He was wounded for our transgressions and brought as a lamb to the slaughter; he was cut off for the transgression of my people, and his soul was made an offering for sin.
precepts.point: Isaiah 53 cannot be speaking of David, who was already dead in Isaiah's day; it speaks of Jesus Christ, cut off out of the land of the living for the transgression of the people, the ultimate sacrifice.

note.label: Numbers 29: The Feasts of the Seventh Month

precepts.why:
We fast on the day of atonement without the sacrifices, because the atonement is now Christ. “But he was wounded for our transgressions, he was bruised for our iniquities: the chastisement of our peace was upon him; and with his stripes we are healed. All we like sheep have gone astray; we have turned every one to his own way; and the Lord hath laid on him the iniquity of us all.” The Lord laid on him the iniquity of us all, just as the priest laid the sins of the nation on the sacrifice of Leviticus 16.

“He was oppressed, and he was afflicted, yet he opened not his mouth: he is brought as a lamb to the slaughter, and as a sheep before her shearers is dumb, so he openeth not his mouth.” He was brought as a lamb to the slaughter, the ultimate sacrifice; that is why the veil rent in two when he died.

“for he was cut off out of the land of the living: for the transgression of my people was he stricken.” This cannot be speaking of David, who was already dead in Isaiah's day; it speaks of Jesus Christ, cut off out of the land of the living for the transgression of the people. “Yet it pleased the Lord to bruise him; he hath put him to grief: when thou shalt make his soul an offering for sin, he shall see his seed, he shall prolong his days, and the pleasure of the Lord shall prosper in his hand.” His soul was made an offering for sin, the sin offering of atonement.

precepts.text: Behold the Lamb of God, which taketh away the sin of the world; Christ is the atonement now.
precepts.point: Isaiah 53 cannot be speaking of David, who was already dead in Isaiah's day; it speaks of Jesus Christ, cut off out of the land of the living for the transgression of the people, the ultimate sacrifice.

note.label: Numbers 29: The Feasts of the Seventh Month

precepts.why:
The kid of the goats for a sin offering and the sin offering of atonement are laid aside in captivity, because the atonement is now Christ. “The next day John seeth Jesus coming unto him, and saith, Behold the Lamb of God, which taketh away the sin of the world.”

Behold the Lamb of God, which taketh away the sin of the world: the lamb brought to the slaughter on whom the Lord laid the iniquity of us all. That is why we fast on the tenth day of the seventh month without the sacrifices.

precepts.text: The fifteenth day of the seventh month shall be the feast of tabernacles for seven days; the first day an holy convocation, and the eighth day a solemn assembly with no servile work.
precepts.point: Leviticus 23 shows what this feast is: all that are Israelites born shall dwell in booths seven days, that your generations may know that the Most High made the children of Israel to dwell in booths when he brought them out of the land of Egypt. That is why once a year, around October, you will see us out in the wilderness in tents, eight days counting the solemn assembly, those of us able to get the time off; all our feast days are memorials of what the Lord did for us.

note.label: Numbers 29: The Feasts of the Seventh Month

precepts.why:
“And on the fifteenth day of the seventh month ye shall have an holy convocation; ye shall do no servile work, and ye shall keep a feast unto the Lord seven days.” Leviticus 23 names this feast.

“The fifteenth day of this seventh month shall be the feast of tabernacles for seven days unto the Lord. On the first day shall be an holy convocation: ye shall do no servile work therein. Seven days ye shall offer an offering made by fire unto the Lord: on the eighth day shall be an holy convocation unto you; and ye shall offer an offering made by fire unto the Lord: it is a solemn assembly; and ye shall do no servile work therein.”

The feast of tabernacles: the first day an holy convocation, seven days of offerings made by fire, of which the thirteen bullocks, two rams, and fourteen lambs of Numbers 29 are the first day's, and the eighth day a solemn assembly with no servile work. That is why our time in the wilderness is eight days counting the solemn assembly.

precepts.text: A statute for ever in your generations: ye shall dwell in booths seven days, that your generations may know that I made the children of Israel to dwell in booths when I brought them out of Egypt.
precepts.point: Leviticus 23 shows what this feast is: all that are Israelites born shall dwell in booths seven days, that your generations may know that the Most High made the children of Israel to dwell in booths when he brought them out of the land of Egypt. That is why once a year, around October, you will see us out in the wilderness in tents, eight days counting the solemn assembly, those of us able to get the time off; all our feast days are memorials of what the Lord did for us.

note.label: Numbers 29: The Feasts of the Seventh Month

precepts.why:
Leviticus 23 shows what the feast of the fifteenth day of the seventh month is. “And ye shall keep it a feast unto the Lord seven days in the year. It shall be a statute for ever in your generations: ye shall celebrate it in the seventh month. Ye shall dwell in booths seven days; all that are Israelites born shall dwell in booths.”

“That your generations may know that I made the children of Israel to dwell in booths, when I brought them out of the land of Egypt: I am the Lord your God.” A statute for ever in your generations, so that your generations may know what the Most High did when He brought Israel out of Egypt.

That is why once a year, around October, you will see us out in the wilderness in tents, eight days counting the solemn assembly, those of us able to get the time off. All our feast days are memorials of what the Lord did for us.

precepts.text: Present your bodies a living sacrifice, holy, acceptable unto God, which is your reasonable service.
precepts.point: If ye love him, keep his commandments, and he will send the Comforter, the Spirit of truth, which the world cannot receive; the Holy Ghost teaches all things and brings all things to remembrance, and that spirit is how this truth is understood in these last days.

note.label: Numbers 29: The Feasts of the Seventh Month

precepts.why:
All the sacrifices of the seventh month were for the set feasts of the Lord, and they came “beside your vows, and your freewill offerings”, which carried sacrifices of their own. The feast days were wrapped in offerings from the sabbath to the solemn assemblies, and that is why Paul wrote, let no man judge you in meat or in drink.

What is left for us is better. Paul beseeches the brethren “by the mercies of God, that ye present your bodies a living sacrifice, holy, acceptable unto God, which is your reasonable service.” The bullocks and rams are gone; the body is the sacrifice now.

Keeping the feast days is how that body is presented. Telling your employer months ahead that you need the day of atonement or the tabernacles off, and helping supply the feasts, is presenting the body a living sacrifice. That is the reasonable service the set feasts ask of us today.

precepts.text: Keeping the law brings offerings enough; departing from wickedness and forsaking unrighteousness is the propitiation now.
precepts.point: If ye love him, keep his commandments, and he will send the Comforter, the Spirit of truth, which the world cannot receive; the Holy Ghost teaches all things and brings all things to remembrance, and that spirit is how this truth is understood in these last days.

note.label: Numbers 29: The Feasts of the Seventh Month

precepts.why:
Every set feast in Numbers 29 came with its burnt offerings, meat offerings, drink offerings and peace offerings. Ecclesiasticus shows what stands in their place: “He that keepeth the law bringeth offerings enough: he that taketh heed to the commandment offereth a peace offering.”

“He that requiteth a good turn offereth fine flour; and he that giveth alms sacrificeth praise.” The fine flour of the meat offering and the sacrifice of praise are now a good turn requited and alms given.

“To depart from wickedness is a thing pleasing to the Lord; and to forsake unrighteousness is a propitiation.” Departing from wickedness and forsaking unrighteousness is the propitiation now. Keeping the law brings offerings enough, so the feasts are kept without the animal sacrifice.

precepts.text: What God before had shewed by the mouth of all his prophets, that Christ should suffer, he hath so fulfilled.
precepts.point: If ye love him, keep his commandments, and he will send the Comforter, the Spirit of truth, which the world cannot receive; the Holy Ghost teaches all things and brings all things to remembrance, and that spirit is how this truth is understood in these last days.

note.label: Numbers 29: The Feasts of the Seventh Month

precepts.why:
Why are the sacrifices of the set feasts no longer brought? “But those things, which God before had shewed by the mouth of all his prophets, that Christ should suffer, he hath so fulfilled.”

The prophets showed before that Christ should suffer, and he has so fulfilled it. His suffering did away with the law of animal sacrifice. The feasts of the Lord remain; what Christ fulfilled is the burnt offerings, meat offerings, drink offerings and peace offerings that were tied to them, so what is left for us is the living sacrifice of the body.

precepts.text: If ye love me, keep my commandments; and the Father shall give you another Comforter, the Spirit of truth, whom the world cannot receive.
precepts.point: If ye love him, keep his commandments, and he will send the Comforter, the Spirit of truth, which the world cannot receive; the Holy Ghost teaches all things and brings all things to remembrance, and that spirit is how this truth is understood in these last days.

note.label: Numbers 29: The Feasts of the Seventh Month

precepts.why:
Moses told the children of Israel “according to all that the Lord commanded Moses.” Christ puts the same charge on us: “If ye love me, keep my commandments.” Keeping the set feasts is keeping his commandments.

With it comes a promise: “And I will pray the Father, and he shall give you another Comforter, that he may abide with you for ever; Even the Spirit of truth; whom the world cannot receive, because it seeth him not, neither knoweth him: but ye know him; for he dwelleth with you, and shall be in you.”

The world cannot receive that Spirit of truth, because it neither sees him nor knows him. Those who love Christ and keep his commandments know him, for he dwells with them. That spirit is how the feasts of the seventh month, and the sacrifices that went with them, are understood in these last days.

precepts.text: The Comforter, which is the Holy Ghost, shall teach you all things, and bring all things to your remembrance.
precepts.point: If ye love him, keep his commandments, and he will send the Comforter, the Spirit of truth, which the world cannot receive; the Holy Ghost teaches all things and brings all things to remembrance, and that spirit is how this truth is understood in these last days.

note.label: Numbers 29: The Feasts of the Seventh Month

precepts.why:
“But the Comforter, which is the Holy Ghost, whom the Father will send in my name, he shall teach you all things, and bring all things to your remembrance, whatsoever I have said unto you.”

The Holy Ghost teaches all things and brings all things to remembrance. That is how the set feasts, the vows, the freewill offerings and the sacrifices beside them are opened up to us now: not by a priest at the altar but by the Spirit of truth, sent by the Father to those who love Christ and keep his commandments. That spirit is how this truth is understood in these last days.

points: The first day of the seventh month is an holy convocation, a day of blowing the trumpets, the memorial of blowing of trumpets: no servile work, and a burnt offering of one young bullock, one ram, and seven lambs of the first year without blemish, with their meat offerings and a kid of the goats for a sin offering.

note.label: Numbers 29: The Feasts of the Seventh Month

points: That day is also the new moon, so the offering of the trumpets came beside the burnt offering of the month, the daily burnt offering, and their meat and drink offerings. In a span of fifteen days this month holds the memorial of blowing of trumpets coupled with the new moon, the day of atonement, and the feast of tabernacles.

note.label: Numbers 29: The Feasts of the Seventh Month

points: The tenth day of the seventh month is an holy convocation, a large gathering, wherein ye shall afflict your souls and do no work at all: the day of atonement, instituted as a statute for ever, when the priest made an atonement to cleanse the people from all their sins before the Lord.

To afflict your soul is to fast. The fast the Lord has chosen is a day for a man to afflict his soul, to loose the bands of wickedness, to undo the heavy burdens, to let the oppressed go free, and to break every yoke; that is why we still fast on this day once a year, and why we go out and teach on the day of atonement.

note.label: Numbers 29: The Feasts of the Seventh Month

points: The first day's offering was thirteen young bullocks, two rams, and fourteen lambs of the first year without blemish, with their meat offerings by number and a kid of the goats for a sin offering, beside the continual burnt offering.

note.label: Numbers 29: The Feasts of the Seventh Month

points: On the second day the count came down to twelve young bullocks, with the same two rams, fourteen lambs of the first year without spot, their meat and drink offerings by number, and a goat for a sin offering, beside the continual burnt offering.

note.label: Numbers 29: The Feasts of the Seventh Month

points: The pattern descends a bullock each day: eleven on the third day, ten on the fourth, nine on the fifth, eight on the sixth, and seven on the seventh day, every day with two rams, fourteen lambs, the meat and drink offerings after the manner, and the goat for a sin offering, all beside the continual burnt offering that never stopped.

note.label: Numbers 29: The Feasts of the Seventh Month

points: The eighth day is a solemn assembly, the last day, with no servile work; its offering was one bullock, one ram, and seven lambs of the first year without blemish, with their meat and drink offerings and a goat for a sin offering, beside the continual burnt offering.

note.label: Numbers 29: The Feasts of the Seventh Month

points: All these sacrifices were for the set feasts of the Lord, and they came beside your vows and your freewill offerings, which carried sacrifices of their own. This is why Paul wrote, let no man judge you in meat or in drink; the feast days of the Lord were wrapped in offerings from the sabbath to the solemn assemblies.

If ye love him, keep his commandments, and he will send the Comforter, the Spirit of truth, which the world cannot receive; the Holy Ghost teaches all things and brings all things to remembrance, and that spirit is how this truth is understood in these last days.
